questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Who read the letter sent by Lencho? What did he do then?
questions.answer: A Postman read it and showed it to the Postmaster. Initially he laughed but soon he became serious and decided to gather money and send it to Lencho on behalf of God. He wanted to retain the poor farmer's faith in God.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What did Lencho hope for and why?
questions.answer: Lencho hoped for a good rain as it was much needed for a good harvest of his crop of corn.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What idea does the Postmaster come up with? What did he do to stick to his resolution?
questions.answer: The postmaster wants to retain the farmer's faith in God. Thus he decides to send him the money. However, he cannot arrange the money by himself and so, he collects it from colleagues in the post office.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.chapter: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom
questions.question: Nelson Mandela in his inauguration speech says, "We, who were outlaws not so long ago, have today been given the rare privilege to be host to the nations of the world on our own soil." What is the significance?
questions.answer: Earlier, the White supremacy in South Africa had founded a system of supremacy and people like Mandela who fought for the freedom of the masses were considered outlaws. However, with the end of that system, now a democratic government was being set up and thus, these freedom fighters were now considered as the harbingers of this freedom.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.chapter: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom
questions.question: Mandela said, "People must learn to hate, and if they can learn to hate, they can be taught to love." Discuss.
questions.answer: According to Nelson Mandela, to love comes naturally to the human heart. Since infancy, one experiences love and warmth. However, hatred is taught to us at a later stage. Hatred makes the receiver sad and gloomy. Thus, slowly, the entire society gives up hatred and embraces love.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Describe the young seagull's first flight.
questions.answer: The seagull was starving. When he saw his mother approaching with a fish in its beak, he called out to her but she stopped mid-flight. This provoked the seagull and unaware, it took a flight. Thus, the bird flew and on realizing this, it was glad to have conquered its fear.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: "I'll take the risk." What is the risk? Why does the narrator take it?
questions.answer: The "risk" here refers to not doing the right thing, which is flying back to Paris when he came to know about the storm. Despite being aware of the bad weather, the pilot headed straight into the storm. The pilot wanted to be with his family and have that English breakfast.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: The author says "During our childhood in Goa, the baker used to be our friend, companion and guide." Elaborate.
questions.answer: This tells us that a baker was a respected person. He was well-learned and so, the people sought his advice and confided their secrets in him. He visited the households everyday and supplied freshly baked goods.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: How did Valli save money to travel by bus?
questions.answer: Valli arranged for her bus fare meticulously. She saved the money herself by resisting temptations like peppermints, toys, balloons. She collected the information from the passengers and utilised the time of her mother's nap for the trip.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What does the Buddha say about the world?
questions.answer: According to Buddha the world is affected by suffering, death and decay.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What was Mr. Herriot's strict advice? Did Mrs. Pumphrey agree to his advice?
questions.answer: Mr Herriot was very strict and told Mrs. Pumphrey that if she did not cut on its food and give him more exercise, Tricki would get sick. She agreed to his advice but it was difficult for her to harden her heart.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Why does Anil not hand over Hari Singh to the police?
questions.answer: Anil was a kind man. He knew that Hari had committed the theft but he did not hand him over to the police because when Hari returned the money, he had realized his mistake and was sorry for it.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: How did Griffin become a homeless wanderer?
questions.answer: Griffin's landlord disliked him and tried to eject him. In revenge, Griffin set fire to the house. To get away without being seen he had to remove his clothes. Thus he became a homeless wanderer, without clothes, without money and quite invisible.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What was the cause of Matilda's ruin?
questions.answer: Matilda Loisel was unhappy and longed to join the wealthy upper class. She borrowed a diamond necklace from her friend Jeanne Forestier for a party. She misplaced the necklace and had to work for ten years to repay the debt, only to discover the original was fake.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What mood of the poet is reflected in the poem "Dust of Snow" initially? What images are used?
questions.answer: Initially, the poet is in a sad mood and he is regretful. The mention of the crow and the hemlock tree indicate gloom and sadness. Later, his mood becomes hopeful which shows the transformative power of nature.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: In what way would writing a letter to God help Lencho tide over his crisis?
questions.answer: Lencho had immense faith in God. After his entire crop was destroyed by the hailstorm, he had no other resort than to seek help from God. Thus, Lencho planned to write a letter to god seeking 100 pesos that would help him sow a new crop and feed his family.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: The postmaster had mixed emotions while opening the letter. Explain.
questions.answer: The postmaster was feeling curious and contented while opening Lencho's second letter. He was looking forward to a letter of thanks but he is shocked to read that Lencho complains that the post office staff is a bunch of crooks who have stolen the remaining thirty Pesos.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Why did the night after the rains turn sorrowful for Lencho?
questions.answer: It was a miserable night. The fields were covered in hail, giving them a salt-white appearance, and had destroyed the crop. It indicated that there would be no harvest, and Lencho's family would face starvation.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What are the raindrops compared to and why?
questions.answer: Raindrops are compared to new coins - the bigger ones are ten-cent coins while the smaller are five cent. It is because they promised a good harvest and as such good money to Lencho.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.chapter: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom
questions.question: A society that ________ was born out of human disaster.
questions.answer: all humanity would be proud of

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.chapter: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom
questions.question: The former outlaws were given the privilege of _________.
questions.answer: hosting the nations of the world on their soil

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.chapter: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom
questions.question: The speaker was overwhelmed with the sense of _______.
questions.answer: gratitude

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.chapter: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom
questions.question: The noun form of the word 'confer' is
questions.answer: C

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.chapter: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom
questions.question: "No one is born hating another person because of the colour of his skin, or his background or his religion". Do you agree? Elaborate.
questions.answer: Through his fight for freedom, Nelson Mandela demonstrated how hatred was more of a social construct than a basic human trait. He observed racism among white people fostered socially rather than naturally. Mandela says hatred is a learned, not innate trait. Since love comes more naturally to the human heart, if one could learn to hate, they could also be taught to love.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: "Family played a vital role in the first flight of the young seagull." Give examples.
questions.answer: The seagull's mother played a pivotal role by carrying the fish in its beak and stopping mid-flight in front of the hungry seagull. This pushed the bird to fly out of hunger. The father ignored the coward seagull. The siblings flew around and called him to fly too.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Motivation plays an important role in taking risks in life and in succeeding. Discuss with reference to the pilot of the old Dakota and the young seagull.
questions.answer: Motivation gives us that push to take up risks in life. The young seagull is scared of taking the first flight but immense hunger and the sight of fish in the mother's beak motivate him. The pilot is so eager to reach home that he overlooks the dark storm clouds and flies into them. Both characters take risk only because of great motivating factors.

questions.answer: C

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: The Paris air control did not reply to the pilot's call because __________.
questions.answer: the radio was dead and there was no transmission to the Paris air control.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: "A Baker from Goa" is a nostalgic saga of childhood memories. Comment.
questions.answer: The story evokes nostalgia through vivid childhood memories of the traditional baker's visits. It recalls the excitement of hearing the bamboo's jingle, rushing to meet the baker, and the delight of choosing bread-bangles.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Who are paders and why are they friends of children?
questions.answer: Goa's village bakers, known as paders, sell their bakery products by going from door to door. The children are particularly fond of them as they bring bread bangles and loaves every morning.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: How is the Goan baker still an important part of the life of a Goan village?
questions.answer: A baker holds a significant role. Bakery items are essential components of every social and religious ceremony. The daily life-cycle of a Goan household commences with the cheerful arrival of the baker. Beyond being a baker, he becomes a friend, companion, and guide.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Where is Coorg located? Write any two characteristics of the people of Coorg.
questions.answer: Coorg is located in Karnataka, between Mysore and Mangalore. The people are known for their martial traditions and distinct culture, possibly tracing back to Greek or Arabic origins. They are also famous for their hospitality.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Valour and hospitality are inherent in the people of Coorg. Explain.
questions.answer: The people of Coorg are famous for their bravery. They are known to be of either Arabic or Greek descent. The Coorgis narrate tales of valour of their ancestors and they are allowed to carry firearms without licenses.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What did Pranjol and Rajvir do during the journey? Why?
questions.answer: During their train journey to Assam, Pranjol and Rajvir drank tea and chatted. Rajvir shared interesting facts about tea. Pranjol was calm and read his detective story books throughout the trip as he had travelled this route earlier.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What is the Indian legend about the discovery of tea?
questions.answer: Bodhidharma, an ancient Buddhist ascetic, cut off his eyelids because he felt sleepy during meditations. Ten tea plants grew out of the eyelids. The leaves when put in hot water and drunk banished sleep.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Why did Pranjol not share Rajvir's excitement at seeing the tea gardens?
questions.answer: Pranjol had taken the train to Assam several times earlier. He was familiar with the scenery and the tea plantations. Thus, he was not excited as Rajvir was.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Why did Valli spend her time all alone and what became her favourite pastime?
questions.answer: Valli spent most of her time alone because she had no friends of her age in the neighbourhood. Her favourite pastime was standing outside her door and watching the street in front of her house.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: How did Valli gather the details of the bus journey?
questions.answer: Valli carefully gathered information by listening to conversations among her neighbours and other regular bus riders. She also asked thoughtful questions and learned every detail about the trip.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What stopped Valli from going to the stall to have a drink? What do we learn from this?
questions.answer: Valli just wanted to go on a bus ride and see the surroundings. She did not want to waste money on a drink. Also, getting down in an unknown town was not safe. This shows Valli was mature and responsible.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Whenever we want to achieve something, difficulties always come. What did Valli have to do to go and ride in a bus?
questions.answer: Valli wanted to take the bus but lacked the funds. She saved whatever spare change came her way while restraining herself from splurging on peppermints, toys, balloons. She paid close attention to the bus' timetable and routine. She listened in on chats regarding people's travels. Her efforts allowed her to fulfil her goal.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: The people and surroundings are a great book to learn from. Valli learns a lot from others. Mention the traits of her character which help her.
questions.answer: Valli was eager to know about the timings, fare and route of the bus. She carefully watched the bus and deduced that it crossed the street at regular intervals. She overheard the passengers and gathered information. On her bus trip, she behaved maturely and confidently. She was careful and cautious. The bus journey made her learn a lot of things.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What does Kisa Gotami ask for when she goes from house to house? Does she get it? Why?
questions.answer: Kisa asks for mustard seeds from such a house that has not lost a beloved. She is not able to find such a house because there is no household that has not suffered the pain of losing a beloved to death.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Kisa Gotami went from door to door when her son died. What was the result?
questions.answer: Kisa sought a cure for her son and her quest led her to Buddha. Buddha asked her to get mustard seeds from a house that had not lost a beloved. She failed to find such a house and realized that death is the ultimate truth.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What did Siddhartha Gautama come across by chance when he was about twenty-five years old?
questions.answer: While out hunting, he chanced upon a sick man, then an aged man, then a funeral procession, and finally a monk begging for alms.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What did Kisa Gotami do after the death of her only son?
questions.answer: Kisa Gotami was overwhelmed with sorrow. Unable to come to terms with this loss, she wandered through her neighborhood, holding her lifeless child, and requested everyone she met to provide medicine that could bring her child back to life.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Through the story of Kisa Gotami, what did the Buddha try to preach to the common man?
questions.answer: Buddha reiterated the ultimate truth of life - death. Kisa was a woman whose son died but she could not bear the truth. Buddha asked her to fetch mustard seeds from a household that had not lost a beloved. When Kisa was unsuccessful, she realized that death was the ultimate truth and accepted her son's death.

questions.question: How did Chubukov react when Lomov asked for the hand of his daughter in marriage?
questions.answer: Chubukov was first suspicious and thought that Lomov had come to ask for some money. But when he came to know the real reason he was overwhelmed with joy because he believed Lomov would be a profitable match. He embraced and kissed Lomov.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: How would the tiger behave in the forest?
questions.answer: He would roam around, baring his teeth and scaring the villagers. He would hide behind tall grass, waiting for the prey to pass.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What does the tiger in the zoo do at night?
questions.answer: He hears the siren of the patrol car and looks at the bright stars.

questions.answer: B

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What impression do you form about Amanda in the poem?
questions.answer: Amanda is an innocent young girl. She is immature and dislikes her mother's constant nagging and scolding. Amanda wants to be free and escape her mother's continuous intervention.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Why does Amanda wish to be a mermaid?
questions.answer: Amanda, who is often chastised by her parents for being lazy, imagines herself as a mermaid who lives a carefree existence. Amanda wants to escape from the daily nagging and reprimanding of her parents.

options: could release fire from the mouth
questions.answer: C

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.chapter: The Tale of Custard the Dragon
questions.question: How does the poem 'The Tale of Custard The Dragon' differ from the traditional ballad?
questions.answer: It is fictitious, and has a lesson so it is more of a fable than a ballad.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.chapter: The Tale of Custard the Dragon
questions.question: What did Custard look like?
questions.answer: Custard had big sharp teeth, spikes on his back, and scales all over. His mouth was like a fireplace, and his nose like a chimney. The toenails were sharp like daggers.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.chapter: The Tale of Custard the Dragon
questions.question: How did the other pets celebrate Custard getting rid of the pirate?
questions.answer: Mustard licked Custard while Ink and Blink sang in happiness and danced around Custard.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: The poet conveys beauty as temporary. Explain with reference to the poem 'For Anne Gregory'.
questions.answer: The poet tells Anne that no young man shall ever love her for what she is but for her yellow hair. Anne replies she could dye her hair and then someone would love her for what she was and not for how she looked.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What did an old religious man declare in the poem 'For Anne Gregory'?
questions.answer: He declared that only God loves us for what we are and not for how we appear.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Why was Mr. Herriot shocked at Tricki's appearance?
questions.answer: The doctor was shocked to see Tricki who appeared like a swollen sausage. The pet's legs were invisible. It was listless, had bloodshot eyes and the tongue lolled from the jaws.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: How did Mrs. Pumphrey treat Tricki?
questions.answer: She was liberal with Tricki. Mrs Pumphrey over indulged Tricki, fed it extras between meals and couldn't bear to refuse. She took Tricki along with her for short walks. She pampered it which finally made it sluggish and listless.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: How did Hari Singh justify to himself his stealing Anil's money?
questions.answer: Hari justified his act by thinking that if he would not take it, Anil would waste the money on his friends. Moreover, Anil did not pay Hari so he deserved taking it.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What does the thief say about the different reactions of people when they are robbed?
questions.answer: Greedy people can be robbed easily and they can afford being robbed. However, it is difficult to rob a careless man who doesn't even notice that he has been robbed.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Why did Hari Singh smile in his most appealing way towards the end of the story?
questions.answer: When Anil gave him a wet fifty-rupee note, Hari realized that Anil had forgiven him. This strengthened their mutual bond of trust which gave Hari the hope for a better future.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Trust and compassion can reform a person. Justify in the light of 'The Thief's Story'.
questions.answer: Anil trusts Hari Singh and overlooks the petty thefts committed by Hari. This casual attitude reforms Hari who loses interest in committing thefts. Anil's positive attitude motivates Hari to return the stolen money. Hari feels that the companionship of a person like Anil can make him a well-educated individual.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: How did Ausable get rid of Max without using a weapon?
questions.answer: When Ausable told Max that it was the police at the door, Max got in a hurry. He accepted Ausable's talk of a balcony outside the window and jumped from the window. However, there was no balcony and he jumped to death.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Describe Max as a secret agent.
questions.answer: Max was thin, with average height. He was crafty like a fox. There was nothing menacing about him except his pistol. He visited Ausable to steal important documents. Ausable outwitted Max and made him jump out of the window.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What does the phrase 'honour among thieves' mean? Why does Horace get angry at this phrase?
questions.answer: The phrase means that one thief should respect another. Horace is cheated by another thief and so, he is irritated at being cheated. In the story, one thief outsmarts the other, takes his help, escapes with the booty and gets him arrested.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature

she was in a state of panic
questions.answer: C

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Griffin's landlord tried to eject him because
options: he had set his house on fire
questions.answer: C

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: The boys were surprised to see a barefooted man in London because ______.
options: everybody in London moved around in shoes
it was very cold in London
only a homeless person would walk barefoot
questions.answer: B

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What opinion did Mr. Weiherer have about Ebright?
questions.answer: Mr Weiherer opines that Richard would make an extra effort and would put in extra three to four hours at night doing debate research. He was competitive in a positive sense.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: How did Ebright's mother help him to become a scientist?
questions.answer: His mother was dedicated and encouraging. She recognized his love for science and provided him with resources. She accompanied him to the library and bought equipment including a telescope, microscope, and cameras.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Why did Richard Ebright raise a flock of butterflies?
questions.answer: Richard developed a keen interest for collecting things. By second grade, he had collected all twenty-five species of butterflies found in Pennsylvania. He also started tagging Monarch butterflies.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What lesson did Ebright learn when he did not win anything at a science fair?
questions.answer: He realized that the winners had performed real experiments. He had simply made a neat display of slides. It was the first time he got a hint of what real science was.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Matilda's over-ambitiousness was the cause of her destruction. Justify.
questions.answer: Matilda Loisel is a gorgeous but unhappy young woman who longs to join the wealthy upper class. She borrows a diamond necklace for a party, misplaces it, and is obliged to work for ten years to repay the debt. The necklace turns out to be a fake. If Matilda had remained content, she would not have to bear such a loss.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Education is considered the most important tool for empowering women. Prove in the light of 'Bholi'.
questions.answer: Bholi is an educated independent woman. Due to her education she could refuse marrying a dowry-seeker. Bishamber insults Bholi's father, and Bholi saves him by refusing to marry such a man. She vows to live with her parents and serve them. Education empowered her to make the right decisions.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Bholi was believed to be a 'dumb cow'. What turned her into a fearless, bold and confident girl?
questions.answer: As a child, Bholi was neglected and weak. Her teacher changed her life. The teacher's affection and understanding converted Bholi to Sulekha, a wise, intelligent and educated woman. Bholi started believing in herself, became brave and confident, and stood up against a bad marriage proposal.

questions.question: Think-Tank wants to communicate with the _____ .
questions.answer: D

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.chapter: The Book that Saved the Earth
questions.question: Your Intelligence refers to
questions.answer: D

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Explain the irony in the chapter "A Letter to God".
questions.answer: Lencho's blind faith in God is ironical because he loses practicality. Lencho thinks God has sent him the money which is not possible. He doubts the integrity of the post office staff as the envelope carries only seventy pesos against the hundred he asked for.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: How far would you agree that one's positivity can bring in a spark of brightness even in adverse circumstances?
questions.answer: Being positive can bring a spark of brightness even in difficult times. Lencho's positive attitude and faith in God gave him hope despite having lost everything. He gathered courage to write a letter to God seeking help.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.chapter: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom
questions.question: The system of racial domination has been replaced by a system that:
options: confirms the education of the Blacks
recognises the rights and freedoms of all people
questions.answer: B

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.chapter: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom
questions.question: Explain the feelings of the narrator when he said: "I was overwhelmed with a sense of history."
questions.answer: His mind was full of the happenings of the past, the struggle that they went through to make the day a reality.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.chapter: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom
questions.question: Comment on the kind of society apartheid had created.
questions.answer: A harsh and inhumane society had been created.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Briefly bring out the contrast between the young seagull's initial attempts to fly and his first successful flight.
questions.answer: The young seagull lacks courage and fears his wings won't support him. When starving, the sight of fish in his mother's beak excites him and he takes the first flight. He is initially terrified but realizes he can fly and then flies confidently.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.chapter: From the Diary of Anne Frank
questions.question: The first education of Anne started at ___________.
questions.answer: C

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.chapter: From the Diary of Anne Frank
questions.question: Which one of the following best describes the tone of the given extract?
questions.answer: B

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.chapter: From the Diary of Anne Frank
questions.question: Elaborate on the justification Anne gives for her talkative nature.
questions.answer: Anne says that she can do nothing about her talkative nature because she has inherited the trait from her mother.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: The baker and his family never starved. Elaborate.
questions.answer: Bakery was a profitable profession because baked goods were an essential part of Goan tradition. The baker visited each house twice a day. Bread and other baked goods were staple diet of Goans. The bakers had a Jackfruit-like belly which indicated prosperity.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Why does the author say the presence of the Baker's furnace in the village is absolutely essential?
questions.answer: There was a bakery in every village, indicating the importance of baked goods in Goan cuisine. Various preparations were part of festivals and occasions. Cakes and bolinhas for Christmas, sandwiches for engagements, wedding gifts included bol.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: The most laid back individuals become converts to the life of high-energy adventure. Elaborate with reference to Coorg.
questions.answer: Coorg has abundance of serene landscapes. One can participate in adventure sports like trekking, river rafting, rock climbing and mountaineering. Even the most laid back individuals feel energised and get tempted to participate.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Coorg has been defined as a 'piece of heaven' by the writer. Justify.
questions.answer: Coorg has stunning natural beauty with rolling hills, lush coffee plantations, colonial bungalows under tree canopies. There are cascading waterfalls, walking trails, a panoramic view from the Brahmagiri hills.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Which of the following is not a reason why Mijbil came on to Maxwell's bed in the small hours?
options: He had started taking interest in his surroundings
He was becoming friendly with Maxwell
He wanted to play with Maxwell on his bed
questions.answer: C

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Maxwell says Mijbil was neither hostile nor friendly, he was simply aloof. Give reasons.
questions.answer: Mijbil was in unfamiliar surroundings, he needed time to adjust and feel comfortable around Maxwell, thus showing indifference as a natural response to the change in his setting.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Mijbil turned out to be a playful pet. Elaborate.
questions.answer: Mijbil enjoyed playing with water, marbles and ping-pong balls. While out for a walk, it would run along the wall of the school and gain attention of teachers and students. It was lively and engaging.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What message might the Buddha's story hold for those who are in positions of power and privilege?
questions.answer: The story imparts the message that death is the ultimate truth and is common to all irrespective of power and privilege. Every human is a mortal and all power, wealth and relatives are left behind.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: "Oh, what a burden, Lord, to be the father of a grown-up daughter!" Explain what this conveys about Chubukov.
questions.answer: The line indicates that a father faces challenges while fulfilling his responsibility towards a grown-up daughter. Chubukov has to perform his parental duty but his daughter has a mind of her own, making him feel burdened.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What argument do Lomov and Natalya give over the superiority of their dogs?
questions.answer: Lomov insists Squeezer is superior, praising his pedigree and hunting abilities, while Natalya defends Guess, asserting his superiority. Their argument escalates into a larger conflict, reflecting their competitive nature.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Justify the title of the play 'The Proposal'.
questions.answer: Lomov wants to propose to Natalya but beats about the bush, speaking irrelevantly. Natalya thinks he has come to claim meadows and quarrels. After Chubukov reconciles, Natalya learns he came to propose. The proposal is made and accepted.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: It is our attitude towards a situation that makes it positive or negative. Express with reference to 'Dust of Snow'.
questions.answer: The symbols of sadness and despair - the crow and the hemlock tree - prove to be auspicious and bring a positive change in the poet's mood. It is the poet's attitude which considers these bad omens to be good for him.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: The poem "A Tiger in the Zoo" moves from the zoo to the jungle and back again. What effect does the poet want to bring out?
questions.answer: The poet contrasts the tiger's natural habitat with its captivity. This underscores the confinement and loss of freedom, highlighting the contrast between its wild nature and restricted existence. It evokes pity and raises awareness about human intervention on wild animals.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the speaker's disposition while describing the Chameleon?
questions.answer: B

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the speaker's attitude towards the boy's reaction to losing his ball?
options: indifferent as the ball is inexpensive
sympathetic, understanding the depth of the boy's loss
questions.answer: B

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.chapter: The Tale of Custard the Dragon
questions.question: Describe the pirate who comes through the window.
questions.answer: The pirate held a shining cutlass between his teeth and held two pistols, one in each hand. He was dressed in all black, and one of his legs was a wooden stump.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.chapter: The Tale of Custard the Dragon
questions.question: What character trait is revealed of Custard when he accepts that the other animals are braver than him?
questions.answer: Custard was revealed to be a character full of humility. Although known to be extremely timid, the entire household witnessed his bravery and couldn't believe their eyes.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What excuses did Mrs. Pumphrey make about Mr. Herriot's advice?
questions.answer: Mrs Pumphrey said she was concerned about Tricki being listless due to malnutrition. She fed it little extras between meals, supplemented with malt and cod-liver oil, added Horlicks at night, and couldn't refuse cream cakes. Hodgkin the gardener was ill and couldn't take Tricki for games.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What did Rajvir see from the train window that fascinated him?
questions.answer: Rajvir saw a magnificent view of green paddy fields giving way to tea bushes. Against the backdrop of densely wooded hills, a sea of tea bushes stretched as far as the eye could see with doll-like figures moving amidst the rows.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Describe the various legends about the discovery of tea as shared by Rajvir.
questions.answer: Rajvir shared two legends about tea discovery. According to the Indian legend, Bodhidharma cut off his eyelids because he felt sleepy during meditations, and ten tea plants grew out of the eyelids. According to the Chinese legend, the emperor of China discovered tea when tea leaves accidentally fell into boiling water.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: The poet uses which poetic device in 'pads of velvet quiet'?
questions.answer: B

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Why was Matilda always unhappy in her early married life?
questions.answer: Matilda was unhappy because she felt she was born for all delicacies and luxuries but suffered from poverty. She had no dresses, no jewels, nothing. She constantly suffered as she hated her circumstances.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Describe the kind of life Matilda and her husband lived after losing the necklace.
questions.answer: After losing the necklace, Matilda and her husband had to replace it with a new one costing thirty-six thousand francs. They had to borrow money, dismiss their servant, move to cheaper quarters, and live a life of poverty. Matilda did all the household work herself, including washing dishes and laundry. This life lasted ten years, after which she looked old and worn.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Destiny had been cruel to Bholi yet she made a place for herself in a conservative society. Discuss.
questions.answer: As the fourth daughter, Bholi was considered an unwanted burden. She lacked confidence and was fearful. But her teacher gave her affection and attention which changed her. She grew into an educated, confident woman who could take a stand for herself and refuse marrying an old dowry-seeker.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Maxwell decides to keep an otter as a pet. Elucidate with reference to commitment.
questions.answer: Keeping a pet requires commitment. When Mijbil played with water in the bathroom, Maxwell had to ensure the pet did not drown. When left unattended, Mijbil hurt itself. Maxwell had to change airlines because some did not fly animals. During the flight, Maxwell endured hardships due to Mijbil's recklessness.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: 'As ripe fruits are in danger of falling early, so mortals when born are always in danger of death.' What moral values did Kisa Gotami learn?
questions.answer: Kisa Gotami was devastated when she lost her child. Buddha demonstrated how pain is universal and death unavoidable. No one is untouched. The wisest person knows not to weep. By acknowledging the fleeting nature of life, one can achieve mental peace and conquer sadness.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.chapter: The Book that Saved the Earth
questions.question: What is the significance of the book in 'The Book that Saved the Earth'?
questions.answer: The book was a nursery rhyme book from Earth that the Martian crew misinterpreted. Think-Tank believed the rhymes contained secret codes and advanced Earth knowledge. The nursery rhymes convinced the Martians that Earth was too advanced to conquer, thus saving Earth from invasion.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: "Coorgi homes have a tradition of hospitality." Elaborate with reference to the chapter.
questions.answer: The people of Coorg are fierce and brave. The families have a tradition of hospitality. The Coorg regiment is the most decorated and General Cariappa, the first Chief of the Indian Army was a Coorgi. They are permitted to carry firearms without a licence.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Why was the young seagull afraid to fly?
questions.answer: The young seagull lacked courage and feared that his wings would not support him. He watched his siblings soar and dive but couldn't overcome the fear. He felt certain that his wings would never support him and he would fall into the deep sea.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Describe the fantasy world of Amanda.
questions.answer: Amanda imagines herself as a mermaid drifting blissfully in the gentle waves, as an orphan wandering freely in the street making patterns with her bare feet, and as Rapunzel living in a tranquil tower without any cares.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What did Valli see on her way back that made her sad?
questions.answer: On her way back, Valli saw a young cow lying dead by the roadside. She recalled seeing the same cow running in front of the bus earlier. This realization about death and the temporal nature of life made her very sad.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What does the poet say about money in 'The Ball Poem'?
questions.answer: The poet says that money is external. No one can buy a ball back, balls will be lost always. The boy is learning about the epistemology of loss - how to stand up after losing something precious.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What does the tiger's 'quiet rage' signify?
questions.answer: The tiger's 'quiet rage' signifies his anger and helplessness at being confined in a cage. He is unable to express his fury openly as he would in the jungle, so his rage is quiet and suppressed.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What difficulty does a novice face in distinguishing beasts of prey according to the poem?
questions.answer: A novice might get confused or nonplussed while trying to distinguish beasts of prey. The poet humorously suggests that one will know a beast by its behaviour towards the observer, especially by whether it eats the observer.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What is the significance of the crow and hemlock tree in the poem 'Dust of Snow'?
questions.answer: The crow and hemlock tree are usually considered symbols of bad omen and sadness. But in the poem, they bring about a positive change in the poet's mood. The poet uses them to show that even negative things can have positive outcomes.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What does the poet mean when he says 'Only God, my dear, could love you for yourself alone'?
questions.answer: The poet means that human beings are attracted by physical beauty. A person may love another for their appearance, but only divine love is unconditional and sees beyond external beauty to the true self within.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What was Richard Ebright's project on butterflies about?
questions.answer: Richard Ebright's project proved that the spots on a monarch butterfly's wings help it to survive. By studying the monarch butterfly's migration patterns and wing spots, he won many science fair competitions.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: How did Griffin's invisibility become a curse for him?
questions.answer: Griffin's invisibility became a curse as he could not be seen but also could not live a normal life. He had to remove his clothes to remain invisible, leaving him homeless and without money. People could feel his presence but not see him, making him a lonely wanderer.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: How did the lady outsmart Horace Danby?
questions.answer: The lady pretended to be the owner of the house and convinced Horace to help her open the safe. After he opened it, she took the jewels and left. Later, Horace was arrested because his fingerprints were found at the scene. The lady was actually a thief herself.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What changes did Mr. Herriot observe in Tricki after a few days of treatment?
questions.answer: After a few days of treatment with plenty of exercise and no food, Tricki started showing signs of recovery. He became more active, his eyes brightened, and he began to enjoy the company of other dogs. He regained his energy and health.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Describe the initial meeting between Hari Singh and Anil.
questions.answer: Hari Singh met Anil at a wrestling match. Anil was watching the match and Hari approached him, trying to win his sympathy. Anil offered to take Hari home and later gave him food and shelter.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: How did Ausable describe the balcony outside his window?
questions.answer: Ausable described a non-existent balcony outside his window. He calmly told Max that the balcony was there and that this was the second time someone had entered his room through that balcony. This made Max believe the balcony was real, leading to his fatal jump.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What argument about dogs do Lomov and Natalya have?
questions.answer: Lomov claims his dog Guess is better than Natalya's Squeezer. He argues that Squeezer is overshot and has weak hindquarters. Natalya defends her dog fiercely, and the argument becomes personal and heated.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.chapter: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom
questions.question: What did Nelson Mandela mean by 'the oppressor too is not free'?
questions.answer: Mandela meant that oppression not only deprived the oppressed of their freedom but also imprisoned the oppressor in a cage of prejudice and hatred. Both the oppressor and the oppressed are robbed of their humanity.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What was Lencho's only hope after the hailstorm destroyed his crop?
questions.answer: Lencho's only hope was his faith in God. He believed that God would help him and his family survive. He decided to write a letter to God asking for 100 pesos to sow new crops and feed his family.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What does the poet Walt Whitman find admirable about animals according to the poem 'Animals'?
questions.answer: The poet finds that animals are placid and self-contained. They do not complain about their condition, do not weep for their sins, do not make him sick discussing duty, and do not kneel to others. They show their relations to the poet, and he accepts them.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: According to the poem 'Animals', what do animals not do?
options: they do not complain about their condition
they show their relations to the poet
questions.answer: C

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What does the poet desire in the poem 'Animals'?
questions.answer: The poet desires to live among animals because they are so peaceful and self-contained. He wants to turn and live with animals as they are better than humans in many ways.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Why did the lawyer go to New Mullion?
questions.answer: The lawyer went to New Mullion to serve a summons on Oliver Lutkins, who was needed as a witness in a law case.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Who was Bill? How did he help the lawyer?
questions.answer: Bill was a hack driver who met the lawyer at the railway station. He helped the lawyer search for Oliver Lutkins by taking him to various places and introducing him to different people who supposedly knew Lutkins.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What was the truth about Oliver Lutkins that the lawyer discovered later?
questions.answer: The lawyer later discovered that the hack driver himself was Oliver Lutkins. Bill had cleverly tricked the lawyer by pretending to help him search for Lutkins while actually fooling him all along.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Why did the postmaster decide to reply to Lencho's letter?
questions.answer: The postmaster decided to reply to Lencho's letter because he wanted to keep Lencho's faith in God alive. He collected money from his colleagues and sent 70 pesos to Lencho as if it were from God.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.chapter: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom
questions.question: How did Mandela's perspective on freedom change as he grew older?
questions.answer: As a child, Mandela's freedom was the freedom to run in the fields and swim in the stream. As a young man, he wanted transitory freedoms. But as an adult, he realized that his freedom was incomplete without the freedom of his people.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What made the young seagull finally take his first flight?
questions.answer: The young seagull was extremely hungry. When he saw his mother carrying a fish, he called out to her. She stopped mid-flight, and out of desperation and hunger, the seagull jumped at the fish and began to fly.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: Why does the narrator say, "I'll take the risk" in the story 'The Black Aeroplane'?
questions.answer: The narrator says this because he is determined to reach home and have an English breakfast with his family. Despite knowing about the storm clouds ahead, he decides to fly through them rather than turn back.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.chapter: From the Diary of Anne Frank
questions.question: What made Anne Frank write a diary?
questions.answer: Anne Frank wrote a diary because she felt she had no true friend with whom she could share her feelings. She decided to write her thoughts in a diary which she named 'Kitty' and considered her best friend.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.chapter: From the Diary of Anne Frank
questions.question: Describe the relationship between Anne Frank and her teacher Mr. Keesing.
questions.answer: Mr. Keesing was annoyed with Anne's talkative nature and gave her extra homework as punishment. However, when Anne wrote clever essays arguing for talking, Mr. Keesing found them amusing and eventually stopped punishing her.

questions.subject: English Language & Literature
questions.question: What is the irony in the poem 'A Letter to God'?
questions.answer: The irony is that while the post office employees collect money for Lencho thinking they are God's messengers, Lencho accuses them of stealing a part of the money sent by God, failing to recognize their help.
